contexts.why: The job is the product's homepage.
An all-day work tool used by experienced keepers.

candidates.name: Night Watch
candidates.why: Experienced keepers scan quickly; a calm, typical page with the log shown first reads fast (E001, E002).
do: a real log screen in the first view
differentiate: a night view that keeps the room dark
candidates.palette: deep navy with one amber accent

candidates.name: Logbook
candidates.why: The weekly summary is read by harbour authorities; an editorial page carries the record's weight (E005).
do: serif headlines over a quiet grid
differentiate: the log page as the main picture
candidates.palette: paper white with ink and a harbour green

candidates.name: Signal
candidates.why: Clear signifiers keep scanning fast (E055); a flat page with strong buttons suits a buying audience.

recommended.reason: Keepers are experts on long night shifts; the calm, dense log-first page fits them best.

taste.note: Fixture run: the fixture taste file is a stand-in, kept apart from the evidence.

assumptions: Authorities decide on the weekly summary, not the log screen.

expect.text: A product screen or picture in the first view
One main call to action near the top
A short list of features below the fold

stand_out.text: Show a night view of the log
stand_out.why: Keepers work in a dim room; no fixture site shows a dark view.

stand_out.text: Lead with the record, not with claims
stand_out.why: The fixture sites lead with slogans.

marks.description: The name set in a plain sans.
A fixture circle beside the name.
No mark on the fixture page.
